outline.description: Outlines how recent large language models struggle mathematically compared with proprietary systems; introduces the Central contribution of DeepSeekMath—a family built atop Code‑trained LLMs adding over ten billion math tokens sourced safely from Common Crawl—and its core techniques such as Group Relative Policy Optimization.
subtopics: Gap between closed‑source giants and open repositories
"DeepLearn‑Cod‑math" pipeline stitching corpus → base model → instruction ↔ reinforcement learning.

outline.description: "DeepSeekMath Corpus" construction begins with OpenWebMath seeds trained through fastText classifiers trained iteratively over Common Crawl domains until five‐fold growth reaches twelve hundred billion tokens.

"Pretrain‑on‑corpus” study comparing DenseWeld’s Small Model (.83 B parameters) trained independently on four available maths corpora demonstrates superior performance whenever trained on “DeepSeekMath”, confirming both magnitude–quality relationship.

"DeepSeekCoderBase‑v1\.5 (7 B)" serves as starting checkpoint thanks to its coding capacity—illustrated through ablation studies demonstrating that starting-from-code gives higher mathematical IQ than general pre‑train.
subtopics: "Learning rate schedule”, batch sizing ÷ context length
"Checkpoint initialization” grants head start over Mistral 7 B.
"Analysis” shows complete elimination of catastrophic forgetting.
